title: The Narrow Bell
verdict: Miles Finch was responsible for the disappearance of a donor pledge card.
intent: Miles Finch wanted to conceal that the largest pledge had been promised to the wrong campaign.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the fundraising coordinator handled the folder after the printer jam.
Remove a donor pledge card from its checked location.
Hide the item in a floral sample book with a slit behind the cover.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a donor pledge card disappeared from a hospital charity office before a fundraising gala.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the printer jammed during the donor announcement rehearsal.
The physical trace was paper fibers under the sample-book clasp.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a silver letter opener with adhesive on its edge.
The item could be concealed in a floral sample book with a slit behind the cover.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the fundraising coordinator knew the sample book had been used to hide spare pledge cards.
distractor_cues: an accountant upset about budget errors
a photographer moving folders for staging
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
